correctness.rationale: All-time three-periodic configurations on a connected GHM graph are exactly globally rotating colorings with a successor-color neighbor at every vertex. On K_3 Cartesian K_n, fixing exact row color palettes makes each column independent. Inclusion-exclusion on subpalettes proves a finite sum with 19^3 terms for every positive n. An exact finite coefficient certificate enumerates these 6859 triples and determines precisely twelve nonzero bases, proving the closed formula for all n, not by numerical extrapolation. A separate literal GHM F^3 computation independently exhausts all 3^(3n) states through n=4 (531441 at n=4), verifying 6, 72, 2562, 119880. Three rotations per temporal orbit and the second-largest base 18 establish orbit and asymptotic results.

originality.rationale: The successor-neighbor three-cycle criterion is prior general theory. Full inspection of the published two-row K_2 Cartesian K_n census finds the distinct five-base formula, not the new twelve-base K_3 Cartesian K_n result. Full subdivision census is not a rook-graph result and does not imply this coefficient evaluation. The 2016 arbitrary-graph GHM paper establishes general synchronization/activity criteria, not a three-row rook count; its sections and results show no rook or line-graph special enumeration. Relevant indexed record and web searches for graph/product/line-graph/succession aliases gave no matching exact formula. Unindexed priority remains a risk, not a proof of priority.

value.rationale: Three-row rook graphs, equivalently line graphs of K_{3,n}, are natural highly symmetric excitable networks. The exact width-uniform twelve-exponential population and temporal orbit count expose a higher-row phase enumeration beyond the two-row matched-clique result. In the leading probability correction, coefficient 9 replaces the known two-row coefficient 6, quantifying a concrete change in nonperiodic-at-initial-time frequency. The fact is a natural complete exact invariant for this family, a useful baseline for later transient-basin work, not an arbitrary finite slice or unsupported universality claim.
